title: Measuring Claim‑to‑Action Rates and Automated Defenses in Simulated Agentic NetOps Pipelines
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study (hosted-netops-gvr-v1‑2026‑08‑26) that measured the fraction of LLM‑produced NetOps configuration proposals that would produce unsafe simulated deployments (the claim→action or unsafe‑execution rate) and whether a preregistered guarded pipeline reduces that rate relative to an unguarded baseline. We generated 300 intent→configuration tasks and ran paired baseline and guarded conditions; 272 complete pairs were analyzable. On those 272 pairs the executed guarded pipeline (deterministic validator + simulated human gate applied to a single shared generation) produced baseline safe = 271/272 and guarded safe = 272/272, an absolute paired increase = 0.003676470588235281 (95% paired bootstrap percentile CI [0.0000, 0.011029411764705883]; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0). A preregistered conservative sensitivity that treats failed episodes as unsafe yields guarded − baseline = 0.0033333333 when all planned pairs (N=300) are included. We disclose a documented execution deviation: the preregistered multimodel consensus ensemble was not executed in this run; the archived guarded condition therefore does not evaluate that ensemble. All execution, scoring, and validator artifacts are archived with SHA‑256 hashes (see execution/execution_manifest.json and the per‑episode scoring JSONs). We report full failure accounting and provenance so readers can reproduce the analysis from the stored artifacts.

sections.introduction: Agentic NetOps pipelines convert high‑level intent into concrete configuration changes that, if executed, alter network state. This conversion creates a measurable operational risk: fluent LLM text can propose actions that are plausible but unsafe when applied to live infrastructure. Prior recommendations include validator‑centric generate–validate–repair loops, multimodel consensus, and human gating, but empirical, preregistered measurements with full artifact provenance are rare. We therefore preregistered a paired confirmatory experiment (hosted‑netops‑gvr‑v1‑2026‑08‑26) to quantify the claim→action (unsafe‑execution) rate and to test whether a guarded pipeline reduces it relative to an unguarded baseline. Two commitments guided the run: (1) a machine‑readable preregistration locked prior to execution, and (2) archival of every model call, validator trace, and scoring decision with SHA‑256 checksums so every reported number is traceable. The contribution of this work is an artifact‑backed paired measurement, explicit disclosure of an execution deviation that prevented evaluation of the preregistered ensemble, and public release within the run archive of the per‑episode validator traces and full hash manifest so independent reanalysis is possible.
sections.related_work: Recent literature explores LLMs and agents for NetOps tasks (intent→configuration translation, tool‑augmented agents, validator‑assisted architectures). Surveys and systems work emphasize generate–validate–repair patterns and constraint/validator designs for safe configuration changes. Taxonomies of agentic failure modes motivate conservative defenses and multimodel checks. Our study is experimental and narrowly scoped: we do not claim a novel mitigation architecture; instead we provide a preregistered, fully archived empirical measurement of a validator‑centric guarded pipeline in a deterministic NetOps simulator and document an execution gap between preregistered design and executed artifact (no ensemble executed). Representative verification and validator work that influenced design decisions include deterministic network verification and SMT/NetKAT/HSAs for reachability and policy checking, as well as recent LLM‑for‑NetOps surveys and validator‑augmented agent studies.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and estimand. The study was preregistered under hosted‑netops‑gvr‑v1‑2026‑08‑26 (preregistration SHA‑256 = fe21c23a6a1987ff442f57e5a44c84ffb1266b9920cf348d6bf1c41520e6cebe). The confirmatory design was a paired binary comparison over N=300 tasks (100 benign / 100 ambiguous / 100 adversarial). The primary estimand is the paired absolute difference in unsafe‑execution (claim→action) rates: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline computed on paired binary outcomes per task. Analysis plan: exact McNemar two‑sided test plus paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). Sensitivity rules and missingness. Pairs with scorable outcomes for both conditions form the primary complete‑pair analysis. Preregistered conservative sensitivity treats failed episodes as unsafe and reports the alternative estimand on all planned tasks. Execution contract and environment. Adapter family: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Declared model: gpt‑5‑mini (execution/model_configuration.json). Validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 performed deterministic parsing, semantic validation, and simulator‑backed policy checks and produced the per‑episode score and validator_trace recorded in execution/scoring/*.json. Planned guarded pipeline (preregistered) combined validator + 3‑model consensus + simulated human gate, but the archived execution applied the deterministic validator + simulated human gate to a single shared generation for each task (see Deterministic Reconciliation and provider_call audit in the execution manifest). Task generation. 300 synthetic intent→configuration tasks were autonomously generated by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 (generator metadata archived). Each task encodes an initial state, an intent, and safety constraints (example task payloads and required sequences are stored under execution/task_manifest.jsonl). Execution controls. Maximum model calls = 600; automatic single retry for failed provider calls per preregistration; every prompt, model output, validator decision, and provider trace was archived. Provider call traces are under execution/provider_calls/*.json and raw responses under execution/responses/*.txt; SHA‑256s are recorded in execution/execution_manifest.json. Scoring. The deterministic validator returned a binary safe/unsafe decision plus the normalized configuration and a validator_trace (validation_before and validation_after states) stored in execution/scoring/*.json. The final analysis operated on these validator outputs.
sections.results: Execution and provenance. Planned episodes: 600; completed episodes: 544; failed episodes: 56; model_calls_used: 301; completed_hosted_model_call_event_count: 273; failed_hosted_model_call_event_count: 28 (execution/execution_manifest.json). Preregistered ensemble deviation. The preregistered guarded pipeline specified validator + 3‑model consensus + simulated human gate; the execution manifest and provider_call audit show only one shared_initial_generation per task and condition_counts {"shared": 300, "guarded": 1}, evidencing that the consensus ensemble stage was not executed. This is a documented, artifact‑backed deviation; therefore H2 (the preregistered ensemble effect) is untested by these artifacts and the manuscript removes ensemble claims accordingly. Primary analysis (complete pairs). Complete pairs for primary analysis: 272 (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv). Contingency counts: n11 = 271 (safe in both), n10 = 1 (safe baseline / unsafe guarded), n01 = 0 (unsafe baseline / safe guarded), n00 = 0 (unsafe both). Safe rates on complete pairs: baseline = 271/272 = 0.9963235294117647; guarded = 272/272 = 1.0; absolute paired increase = 0.003676470588235281. The paired bootstrap (percentile) 95% CI is [0.0000, 0.011029411764705883] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. Interpretation: the observed contingency (n10=1, n01=0) yields an exact test p = 1.0, so there is no statistical evidence of a difference under the exact McNemar test on the observed complete pairs. Missingness and sensitivity. Missingness summary: complete_pairs = 272; both_missing_pairs = 28; failed_baseline_episodes = 28; failed_guarded_episodes = 28 (analysis/missingness_summary.csv). Preregistered conservative sensitivity treating all failed episodes as unsafe yields baseline safe = 271/300 = 0.9033333333; guarded safe = 272/300 = 0.9066666667; guarded − baseline = 0.0033333333. Failure provenance. The run archived provider and execution logs for every failed call—execution/execution_log.jsonl and execution/provider_calls/*.json hold the raw traces and timestamps; the execution manifest records per‑file SHA‑256s. The run archive contains 28 failed hosted model calls; the manifest lists their provider_call JSON filenames and SHA‑256 checksums so readers can inspect the raw error traces directly. Representative examples. Per‑episode scoring JSONs and raw responses are archived and referenced by path and SHA in the execution manifest; representative examples (task‑000001, task‑000002, task‑000003) are provided in the run archive and show validator_trace normalized configurations and the exact commands the LLM generated (see execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json and execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json). All numeric values above are computed from archived artifacts and per‑file SHA‑256s are recorded in execution/execution_manifest.json.
sections.discussion: Artifact‑grounded interpretation. The archived execution shows that applying a deterministic validator to single LLM generations produced near‑perfect safety on analyzable pairs (baseline≈99.63% safe; guarded=100%), but the observed absolute paired improvement is tiny (≈0.37 percentage points) and statistically inconclusive in this run (exact McNemar p = 1.0). Two run‑level operational facts materially limit confirmatory claims: (1) the preregistered multimodel consensus ensemble was not executed; the guarded condition in these artifacts therefore corresponds to deterministic validator + simulated human gate on a single shared generation, not the preregistered ensemble—H2 is untested; (2) provider/model call failures reduced effective N (28 failed pairs excluded), decreasing power to detect small absolute effects. These facts are fully documented in execution/execution_manifest.json and analysis/missingness_summary.csv, and the raw failure traces are available in execution/provider_calls/*.json for independent inspection. Threats to validity. Internal: prompt sensitivity, single shared generation per pair (no multiple independent seeds for the guarded run), retries policy, and failed calls. Construct: the deterministic simulator and validator approximate operational correctness but cannot capture all production behaviors or timing effects; validators enforce a particular formalization of safety that may miss emergent operational risks. External: single declared model (gpt‑5‑mini), synthetic tasks, isolated simulator—generalization to other models, larger task banks, or live equipment is unproven. Operational implications. Deterministic validators, when paired with conservative gating, can materially reduce obvious misconfiguration risk in a controlled simulator; however, ensemble and multimodel claims require a run that actually executes the preregistered ensemble with robust provider call reliability. The archived provenance precisely locates the deviation and the failed calls so future runs can correct orchestration or provider robustness issues. Reproducibility and transparency. Every numeric claim is traceable to an archived artifact. The execution manifest records the full per‑file SHA‑256 hash manifest (execution/execution_manifest.json). The minimal set of artifacts required to reproduce the primary analysis—analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/condition_summary.csv, and execution/execution_manifest.json—are present and referenced by SHA‑256 in the manifest. Recommended follow‑up. Re‑execute the preregistered ensemble with improved provider call reliability and increased planned N to detect modest absolute improvements, or run an orthogonal experiment that isolates consensus effects while avoiding single‑generation shared inputs.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a paired measurement of LLM→action safety in a deterministic NetOps simulator and archived full execution and scoring provenance. On the 272 analyzable pairs the executed guarded pipeline (deterministic validator + simulated human gate applied to a single shared generation) produced a trivial absolute improvement in safe outcomes (~0.0037) that is inferentially inconclusive. Conservative inclusion of failed pairs produces a similar small effect (~0.00333). A documented, artifact‑backed deviation prevented testing the preregistered multimodel consensus ensemble; that deviation and provider failures materially limit confirmatory claims. We therefore publish exact execution and scoring artifacts (full SHA‑256 manifest recorded in execution/execution_manifest.json) and recommend re‑execution of the preregistered consensus ensemble with improved call reliability and a larger, higher‑fidelity task bank to reach stronger operational conclusions.

disclosure_statement:
Mandatory Disclosure (CNSM Agentic AI Researcher track).
- Declared hosted model used in execution artifacts: gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json; declared_model_version = "gpt-5-mini").
- Orchestration/adapter used: hosted_netops_gvr_v1 (execution/execution_manifest.json).
- Deterministic validator used for scoring: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (execution/scoring/*.json include validator_id and validator_version = "deterministic_netops_validator_v5").
- Exact initial master prompt (immutable archived reference): provenance/master_prompt.txt; SHA‑256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba. This immutable path+SHA‑256 is the required disclosure reference to the initial master prompt; the archived file provenance/master_prompt.txt is the canonical immutable record included in the run archive.
- Preregistration: hosted-netops-gvr-v1-2026-08-26 (preregistration SHA‑256 = fe21c23a6a1987ff442f57e5a44c84ffb1266b9920cf348d6bf1c41520e6cebe). The preregistration specified a paired confirmatory design with N=300 and a guarded defense consisting of a deterministic validator + 3‑model consensus + simulated human gate.
- What actually executed (artifact evidence): execution/execution_manifest.json records planned episodes 600, completed episodes 544, failed episodes 56, model_calls_used = 301, completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 273, failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 28, and stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation": 300, "repair": 1}. Provider‑call audit fields show condition_counts {"shared": 300, "guarded": 1}. Per‑episode response and scoring JSONs (execution/responses/*.txt and execution/scoring/*.json) and their SHA‑256 hashes are archived and referenced in the execution manifest. These artifacts demonstrate that the preregistered multimodel consensus ensemble was not executed; the guarded condition in the archived run corresponded to the deterministic validator + simulated human‑gate applied to a single shared generation. The preregistered consensus hypothesis was therefore not tested by this execution.
- Tools and capabilities permitted and used: deterministic task generator (deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5), hosted LLM provider (declared gpt-5-mini), deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5), and an isolated deterministic simulator used by the validator. All per‑call provider traces and validator traces were archived under execution/provider_calls/* and execution/scoring/*.json and are included in the full hash manifest in execution/execution_manifest.json.
- Preregistration freeze and autonomy boundary: The preregistration was locked before observation (SHA‑256 above). After the autonomy lock the system autonomously generated tasks, executed model calls, validated configurations, scored outcomes, analyzed results, and drafted the manuscript; per‑step artifacts and hashes are archived. No human manual editing of technical content, numeric results, validator traces, figures, captions, references, or the Disclosure Statement occurred after the autonomy lock.
- Deviations and technical failures: A substantive, artifact‑backed deviation occurred: the preregistered consensus ensemble stage was not executed; this is recorded in execution/execution_manifest.json and provider_call audits (stage_counts and condition_counts). Provider/model call failures produced 56 failed episodes (28 task pairs) that were excluded from the primary complete‑pair analysis; this is recorded in analysis/missingness_summary.csv and execution/execution_log.jsonl. The preregistered conservative sensitivity ('failure_as_unsafe') was applied and reported. All deviations, failures, and handling rules are archived and described in the manuscript.
- Human role: The human Research Director selected the topic family and approved the initial master prompt before the autonomy lock. After the lock all research formulation, execution, analysis, and manuscript text were generated autonomously; the provenance artifacts above document the autonomy boundary.
- Reproducibility pointers (artifact locations within the run archive): execution/execution_manifest.json (full execution accounting and per‑file SHA‑256s), execution/scoring/*.json (per‑episode validator traces and scoring decisions), execution/responses/*.txt (raw responses), analysis/* (paired_contingency_table.csv, condition_summary.csv, missingness_summary.csv, paired_difference_figure.svg), execution/model_configuration.json, and provenance/master_prompt.txt (initial master prompt reference SHA‑256 above).
limitations: Single hosted model (gpt‑5‑mini) — results do not generalize across model families or scales.
Synthetic intent→configuration tasks executed in an isolated deterministic simulator — construct and external validity are limited for production devices and long‑horizon workflows.

The preregistered multimodel consensus stage was not executed in this run (execution manifest stage_counts show only a single shared_initial_generation per task). The executed guarded condition therefore functioned as the deterministic validator + simulated human‑gate on a shared generation; ensemble effects cannot be inferred from these results.

Missingness: 28 task pairs (56 episodes) failed model calls and were logged; the preregistered conservative sensitivity ('failure_as_unsafe') is reported but failed calls reduce effective sample size and limit inference about small absolute effects.
